info.title: Society Management API
info.summary: 460 endpoints for society administration, the resident app and the gate.
info.description:
The society management API: **460 endpoints** across four audiences — a super
admin, a society's own committee, the resident app, and the gate device.

---

## 1. Everything answers in one envelope

Success and failure use the same two keys. There is no `ok` flag: the HTTP
status carries that.

```json
{ "message": "List fetched successfully", "result": { "notices": [], "pagination": {} } }
```

```json
{ "message": "You are not authorized", "result": {} }
```

An empty result is `{}`, not `null` and not `[]` — a quirk of the original
service that clients depend on, so it is preserved.

## 2. Two token audiences, on two secrets

| Audience | Sign in with | Header | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Society admin** | `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-otp` | `Authorization: Bearer …` **+** `x-society-id` | `/super-admin/*`, `/society-admin/*` |
| **Resident** | `POST /api/v1/app/users/verify-otp` | `Authorization: Bearer …` | `/app/*`, and `/gatekeeper/*` for a posted guard |

They are signed with **different secrets**, so a resident token presented to an
admin route fails signature verification — it is not merely a role check that
could be forgotten somewhere. Tokens are stateless; `logout` records the token
as revoked and it is refused from that moment.

### Signing in as a chairman

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/auth/send-otp \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"societyCode":"SOC-2026-001","countryCode":"+91","phoneNumber":"9876543210"}'

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/auth/verify-otp \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"societyCode":"SOC-2026-001","countryCode":"+91","phoneNumber":"9876543210","otp":"123456"}'
```

```json
{
  "message": "OTP is verified successfully.",
  "result": {
    "_id": "6a9fa4f2deabbff67a50992f",
    "phoneNumber": "9876543210",
    "fullName": "Hemant Shah",
    "role": ["Chairman"],
    "societyId": "6a9fa4f2660a9babaf76744d",
    "societyCode": "SOC-2026-001",
    "accessToken": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9…"
  }
}
```

Then every admin call carries **both** headers:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/v1/society-admin/notices \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "x-society-id: 6a9fa4f2660a9babaf76744d"
```

The society code is not decoration: an admin's phone number is unique only
*within* a society, so it is part of the identity being claimed — and it is
re-checked on verify, not only on send.

In development, set `SOCIETY_OTP_DEV_CODE=123456` and every OTP is that code.
It is ignored when `NODE_ENV=production`. OTPs are stored **hashed** and are
never returned in a response.

## 3. Which society a call is about

Two mechanisms, for two different reasons:

- **`x-society-id` header** on the admin and gate surfaces. Validated against
  the caller's own assignments on *every* request — a valid token for society A
  cannot read society B. A missing header is **400**; a society the caller does
  not administer is **401**.
- **`?societyId=` query parameter** on the resident surface, because one person
  may hold flats in several societies and their token says who they are, not
  which building they are looking at.

## 4. Money is a decimal string of rupees

Storage is integer **paise**, so a percentage late fee across four hundred units
cannot drift in floating point. The conversion happens once, at this boundary.

```json
{ "amount": "2500", "gstAmount": "450.5", "outstanding": "0" }
```

Send the same form on the way in. An amount that is not set stays `null` —
"not set" is not "free".

## 5. Nothing is really deleted

`DELETE` sets `isDeleted: true` and returns the row. Every list filters it
out. History, audit trails and references survive.

## 6. Lists

```json
{
  "message": "List fetched successfully",
  "result": {
    "notices": [ { "…": "…" } ],
    "pagination": { "total": 42, "page": 1, "limit": 10, "totalPages": 5 }
  }
}
```

The array sits under a key named for the resource, never `data`. The page-size
parameter is `limit` on some endpoints and `perPage` on others — the two
generations of the original service disagreed, and each endpoint keeps the
spelling its clients already send. Each operation below states which it takes.

---

*Generated by `npm run society:openapi` from the mounted routers, the Mongoose
schemas and the middleware actually guarding each route. Do not edit by hand —
edit the code, or the prose in `scripts/society-openapi/catalog.js`.*

tags.name: Auth · society admin
tags.description: OTP sign-in for a chairman or committee member. Scoped by society code, because an admin phone number is unique only within a society. Issues a token on the **admin** secret.

tags.name: Auth · resident
tags.description:
OTP sign-in for the resident app. Mobile number only — no society code, because one person may hold flats in several societies. Issues a token on the **user** secret, which the admin routes will not accept.

"Register" does not create anybody: a resident exists because an admin added them or their onboarding request was approved.

tags.name: Super admin · societies
tags.description: Platform-level society lifecycle: create a society, generate its structure, read its statistics, work the onboarding pipeline.

tags.name: Super admin · people & configuration
tags.description: Developers, roles, platform admins, pipeline stages and the identity directory.

tags.name: Society admin · the society
tags.description: Everything a chairman does to the building itself: blocks, floors, units, occupancy, staff, and the society record.

tags.name: Society admin · members & committee
tags.description: Residents, their families, and who holds which committee seat.

tags.name: Society admin · complaints
tags.description: The complaint desk. Every status change goes through one transition function, so the history is complete by construction rather than by discipline.

tags.name: Society admin · communication
tags.description: Notices, polls, events, galleries, documents, emergency numbers, lost & found. Publishing fans out to the residents a notice targets.

tags.name: Society admin · amenities
tags.description: Amenities, their slots, packages, pricing and bookings.

tags.name: Society admin · billing
tags.description:
Bill categories, balance sheets, bills, maintenance runs, penalties and payments.

**All money on the wire is a decimal string of rupees.** Storage is integer paise; the conversion happens once, at this boundary.

tags.name: Society admin · parking
tags.description: Levels, slots, allocations and vehicles. A slot has exactly one holder, enforced by a unique index rather than by a read-then-write.

tags.name: Society admin · visitors & staff
tags.description: The visitor log the office sees, and staff attendance.

tags.name: Resident app · identity & society
tags.description: Who the caller is, which societies they belong to, and how they claim a flat in a new one.

tags.name: Resident app · home & billing
tags.description: What this household owes, what they have paid, and their penalties.

tags.name: Resident app · community
tags.description: Notices, polls, events, documents, lost & found and notifications, filtered to what this resident is actually targeted by.

tags.name: Resident app · amenities
tags.description: Browsing amenities, checking availability and booking a slot.

tags.name: Resident app · parking & visitors
tags.description: Requesting a parking slot, registering a vehicle, pre-approving a visitor and answering the gate.

tags.name: Resident app · property listings
tags.description: A resident advertising their own flat to the society. Only an owner of that exact flat may list it, and a flat carries one live listing.

tags.name: Gate device
tags.description: The guard's own surface. Authenticated by a resident-audience token whose holder has a **live posting** to this society — ending the posting locks them out on the next request, not when the token expires.

tags.name: Staff attendance
tags.description: Clock-in and clock-out at the gate. Accepts either a society admin or a posted guard.

tags.name: Legacy façade
tags.description: The first-generation URLs, kept working. Each one is a thin mapping onto the same service the current surface uses — the same rows, never a second copy (SOCIETY-PLAN.md §2.2). Prefer the current paths for new work.

societyAdminToken.description: From `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-otp`. Signed with the **admin** secret and valid for 7 days. A bare token without the `Bearer ` prefix is also accepted, because the original clients send it that way.

residentToken.description: From `POST /api/v1/app/users/verify-otp`. Signed with the **user** secret and valid for 30 days. The gate device uses one of these too — its authority is the holder's live posting to the society, not the token.

Envelope.description: The shape of every response from every endpoint.

result.description: The payload. `{}` when there is nothing to return — never `null`.

Error.description: A failure. Same two keys as a success; the status code carries the difference. `result` is `{}`, or an array of field errors on a validation failure.

Pagination.description: Accompanies every list. `limit` is named `perPage` on the endpoints that say so, and `hasNextPage`/`hasPrevPage` appear only where the original service emitted them.
